A career can open a door. The visa route still matters.

Australian work pathways are not one single system. Some depend on an invitation and points. Others begin with an employer and a nominated role. Start by seeing which questions belong to each route.

Compare the broad routes

A job offer is not a visa grant.

Occupation eligibility, employer nomination, invitation rounds, and application rules can all affect the next step. This guide is an orientation, not an eligibility check. Verify the details for the visa you are considering.

Two different ways to explore skilled work.

Begin with the mechanism, then check the exact visa stream and current rules.

01

Points-tested and nominated

Some skilled visas use an Expression of Interest in SkillSelect. Depending on the visa, you may need an eligible occupation, a suitable skills assessment, enough points, nomination, and an invitation.

  • 189Skilled Independent, points-tested stream
  • 190Skilled Nominated, with state or territory nomination
  • 491Skilled Work Regional, with eligible nomination or family sponsorship

A points minimum is not a promise of an invitation. Occupations, selection, and nomination settings can differ.

189 Independent 190 Nominated 491 Regional Explore SkillSelect
02

Employer-sponsored

These routes depend on an employer nominating a role, and on both the employer and worker meeting the requirements for the particular visa and stream.

  • 482Skills in Demand, temporary employer-sponsored visa
  • 186Employer Nomination Scheme, permanent visa with different streams
  • 494Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional, for eligible regional roles

A job advertisement or offer does not by itself confirm that a role can be nominated or a visa granted.

A few useful checks before you invest in a pathway.

Do them in this order so you can spot the right questions before paying for assessments or tests.

  1. 01

    Describe the work, not just the job title

    Write down the main tasks, qualifications, and experience behind the role you have in mind. Similar job titles can map differently.

  2. 02

    Check the occupation against the exact visa

    Different visa programs use different occupation lists. The Department's list also identifies codes and, for many occupations, the assessing authority.

    Search the skilled occupation list
  3. 03

    Find out whether a skills assessment is required

    Assessment bodies set their own evidence, timing, and fees. Check the correct authority and current validity rules before arranging an assessment.

    Read about skills assessments
  4. 04

    Check where you can apply from

    If you are already in Australia, check your current visa conditions and the onshore rules for the specific visa. If you are outside Australia, confirm the application and decision location rules too.

    Check visa details and conditions
  5. 05

    Organize the evidence after you know what is relevant

    Keep your own private list of what the official process asks for. Open Path does not collect documents or personal details.

    Use the document planner

If you pay for migration help, check who can provide it.

Australian rules limit who can provide immigration assistance for a fee. Read the Department's guidance and verify a migration agent's registration before you engage them.

Using a registered migration agent
